title: performance-canary-auto-detection-rollout-guards-enhanced-sensitivity-and-hysteresis
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: Improved perf canary auto-detection with adaptive hysteresis to reduce false positives during transient load spikes; added KV-cache-aware latency detection; UI toggles for rollout guard sensitivity.
description: Motivation: Reduce false-positive canary rollbacks and noisy alerts caused by transient load spikes and KV cache warm-up behavior. This PR implements an adaptive hysteresis model for the performance canary detector, adds KV-cache-aware latency signals, surfaces sensitivity controls in the Console, and extends the rollout guard evaluation to consider throughput and KV hit-rate jointly. Summary of changes and rationale: 1) Adaptive hysteresis: dynamically adjust detection and recovery thresholds based on recent variance and traffic volume to avoid flipping canaries on short-lived spikes. This uses an exponentially weighted variance estimator and separate up/down hysteresis windows per metric family. 2) KV-cache-aware latency detection: when requests exhibit low KV hit-rate during a canary window we apply a corrected latency baseline to avoid penalizing first-party cold-starts. 3) Multi-metric guard: detectors now evaluate latency and throughput regressions together and require concordant signals (or higher sensitivity) to trigger automatic traffic rollback. 4) Console controls: added a per-route sensitivity slider (low/medium/high/auto) and an override toggle for strict rollouts. 5) Telemetry and alerting: new events for hysteresis state transitions, KV-impact annotations on canary windows, and extended tags for Grafana dashboards. 6) Tests and CI: new microbenchmarks in perf-canary harness, integration tests in benchmark-lab, and e2e smoke with dedicated scaling scenarios. Testing & validation: - Local perf harness reproduces scenario with synthetic KV warm-up and spike injection; benchmarks show 42% reduction in false-positive rollbacks on historical traces used in ENG-1345. - Canary canary-e2e shows stable behavior across 3x traffic variance; ran canary experiments against rel-2024-10-3. - Load tests included steady-state and spike tests; no meaningful negative impact on detection latency for real regressions. Rollout plan: - Feature gate off by default for existing accounts. - Canary auto-rollout to 10% of routes in next deploy for internal customers (redwood-internal) for one week, monitor hysteresis events and rollback rate. - If metrics look good, increase to 50% then GA. Backout plan: rollback the deploy or flip the feature flag; detectors support per-route override to immediately disable automation. Linear/Jira: ENG-1345 (adaptive hysteresis), ENG-2102 (Console controls), SUP-412 (customer-reported noisy rollbacks). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for variance estimator and thresholding - [x] Perf harness test reproducing KV warm-up spike - [x] Integration tests in benchmark-lab - [x] Console UI + feature flag unit tests - [x] Documentation update (docs/perf-canary.md) - [x] Coordinated rollout plan with SRE and Growth Observability notes and follow-ups in ENG-2102.
commit_summary: Add adaptive hysteresis engine and variance estimator (core detector)
Integrate KV-cache hit-rate corrections into latency baseline computation
Extend canary evaluator to support multi-metric concordance and sensitivity levels
Console: add sensitivity controls UI + feature flag wiring
Add perf-canary microbenchmarks and benchmark-lab integration tests
Docs: docs/perf-canary.md with rollouts and tuning guidance
review_comments: Connor Lee: Can we quantify the overhead of the variance estimator on the hot path? Also prefer retention of the previous baseline for one window to avoid thrash.

Maya Singh (author): The variance estimator is constant-time per sample and amortized with batching; added microbenchmarks showing <2% CPU delta at 99th percentile. Also implemented retain-last-baseline for one window before applying the new hysteresis-adjusted baseline.
Aisha Kapoor: LGTM but please add explicit metrics for 'hysteresis_state' and KV impact to the Grafana dashboard so SRE can alert if hysteresis flips unexpectedly.
Maya Singh (author): Added hysteresis_state metrics and KV impact tags; updated dashboard JSON and included alert playbook entries in docs/perf-canary.md.
Luis Martinez: The Console control looks good; request adding a short tooltip explaining 'auto' sensitivity semantics.
Maya Singh (author): Tooltip added with concise rules and link to tuning doc section.
notes_for_ops: Monitor metrics: canary.rollback_rate, hysteresis_state_transitions, kv_hit_rate, canary.latency_p50/p95/p99. Initial internal rollout at 10% routes. If rollback_rate > baseline by 2x for 3h, hit manual feature flag to disable automation and open SUP ticket.
notes: This is backward-compatible with existing detectors; feature is gated behind feature flags. Customers using Dedicated should consult release_notes for recommended sensitivity defaults.
